results.body:
Filter tasks

You can narrow your task search results directly on the Tasks page using filters, by sorting columns, and by searching specific date ranges or no due date. Filter preferences cannot be saved or set as default, which means you will need to apply the filters again when you leave the Tasks page.

Tip: Scroll to the bottom of the Tasks page and click Expand rows to view expanded rows with full task descriptions.

Apply filters Sort table columns Filter via date range
  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Click Filters.
  3. Sort by your choice of filters and then click Apply filters.
  4. Click Clear filters when you are finished.

Tip: If you need to bulk delete or reassign a deactivated user’s tasks, select All users in the Assigned to field to show all firm users. Then you can sort the Tasks table by the Assigned to column to find the deactivated user’s tasks.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Select Columns.
  3. Check the box next to each column you want to appear in the table and click Update columns.
  4. You can now click and drag columns to move them, click columns to sort by column type, or shorten or lengthen columns by clicking and dragging the column borders.

Tip: Sort tasks by due date to see which tasks are due soon.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Next to the Completed quick filter, click the date fields to select a date range or click the All dates dropdown to filter by pre-set date ranges.

 

Print tasks

When you print a single task, the printed document will show all the task details.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Click the down arrow next to Mark complete and select Print task.

 

Export tasks

When exporting tasks, you can use filters to narrow your task results or export all tasks. Outstanding and completed tasks can only be exported in separate document files.

  1. Go to the main Tasks tab or the Tasks subtab within a matter.
  2. Click either Outstanding or Completed.
  3. Optional: Click Filters to narrow your results.
  4. Scroll down and click Export.
  5. Select either PDF or CSV and then click Export.

 

Set up task feeds

If you want to view your Clio Manage tasks in a calendaring application like Google or Apple iCal, you can set up a one-way task feed sync. 

  1. Go to Tasks.
  2. Select Task feeds.
  3. Follow the steps below depending on if you are using Apple iCal, Google, or another calendaring application:
    • Apple iCal: Click Personal task ics feed (Outlook/iCal) and follow the on-screen prompts to set up the feed.
    • Google or other calendaring applications: Right-click Personal task ics feed (Outlook/iCal) and then select Copy Link Address. Use the link to add your tasks to your preferred calendaring program.

results.name: Record and Export Transactions
results.title: Record and Export Transactions
results.body:
Recording vendor transactions and exporting account data provides your firm with a complete, auditable financial record for every matter. Accurate transaction logs ensure that disbursements to third parties are tracked against the correct client ledger, and exported data provides the raw input needed for external accounting reconciliation.

Note: Users with relevant permissions can record and/or export transactions. Learn more in Roles and Permissions in Clio Manage.

Record transactions

You can record a transaction to track funds moving in or out of an operating account, such as a payment to a vendor, a bank fee, or any other adjustment to your account balance. If the transaction relates to a specific client or matter, completing those fields will let you track and report on it accordingly. When recording a transaction for paying a vendor you can also link the transaction to the related expense to track payment status and keep your accounts accurate.

You can view recorded transactions showing funds out in the transactions table of your operating account, the bank account activity, and in client ledger reports.

  1. Go to Accounts and select an operating account. You can also go to the Transactions subtab in a contact or matter.
  2. Click New transaction.
  3. Complete the required fields.
    • Amount: Enter the amount that will be paid to the vendor as a negative number (e.g., -200).
    • Date: Select the transaction date.
    • Account: Select the appropriate operating account that the funds will be paid from.
  4. Complete the remaining fields as necessary. Adding information to these fields can be useful when viewing transactions and when generating relevant reports.
    • Client and matter fields: If you want to link a hard cost expense entry to the current transaction, you have to select a client and matter. When selected, the Hard cost field appears (see below).

    • Hard cost: When you select a matter with a hard cost expense entry, this field appears. Select the relevant entry from the list.

      Note: The amount entered previously must be equal to or less than (in absolute value) the amount of the hard cost.
      Note: Linking vendor transactions will update the Vendor Bill Status.
    • Source/Destination: When you’ve selected a disbursement, the vendor’s information appears in this field.
    • Invoice reference: Add reference information about the vendor invoice you received.
    • Payment method: Note your payment method (e.g., cash, check).
    • Check or reference no.: Add reference information about your payment (e.g., check number).
    • Description: Enter information about the purpose of the transaction (e.g. "Payment for bill [bill number]").
  5. Click Record transaction.

 

Export transactions

Transaction data can be exported from a single bank account or from a specific matter or contact. Bank account exports support QuickBooks formats for direct integration with accounting software. Matter and contact exports are available in PDF or CSV format.

Export from a bank account

  1. In Clio Manage, click Accounts.
  2. Click Export transactions at the top right.
  3. Select the bank account, date range, and export format.
  4. Click Export Transactions.

 

Export from a matter or contact

  1. Open the matter or contact and click the Transactions tab.
  2. Select the operating or trust account.
  3. Optional: Select a date range.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Export.
  5. Select the file format and click Export.

 

Up next

  • Transfer Funds Between Accounts: Move funds between bank accounts or matters while maintaining compliance.
  • Create and Manage Bank Accounts: Create internal records of your firm's bank accounts.

results.name: Filter and Export Bills
results.title: Filter and Export Bills
results.body:
In Clio Manage, you can filter your bills to find the ones you need, then export them in bulk as PDF or CSV files for your records or a client's. You can also generate a statement of account for one client or all clients to show payments and balances at a glance. This gives your firm a clear, exportable record of billing activity without opening each bill individually.

 

Filter bills

Filter bills from the main Billing page or from a matter or contact's Bills subtab, by client, matter, originating attorney, responsible attorney, the date the bill was sent, the due or issue date range, overdue bills, bill type (trust funds or firm revenue), currency, or custom fields. Search by a bill's ID number in the Search by ID field.

Tip: Add or remove columns and sort by bill issue date or last sent date to find the most recent bills.

  1. Go to Billing, or the Bills subtab in a contact or matter.
  2. Select a bill status quick filter: Draft, Pending approval, Unpaid, Paid, All bills, or Archive.
  3. Optional: Click Columns to show or hide specific columns on the table.
  4. Click Filters.
  5. Select your filter choices and click Apply filters.

 

Export bills

Export all generated bills, only bills with outstanding balances, or bills in specific states, and apply filters to narrow the results further.

  1. Go to Billing.
  2. Select Bills or Outstanding Balances.
  3. Optional: Select a bill state.
  4. Optional: Click Filters, choose your filters, and click Apply filters.
  5. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Export.
  6. Select the export format and click Export.

 

Generate statements of account

A statement of account export shows bill invoice amounts, payments, and balances due on a client's account, including any interest, discounts, and credit notes applied to bills in the total calculation. The export excludes transactions unrelated to bill payments, such as amounts deposited into trust. Generate this export for all clients with approved bills, or for specific clients, and select filters such as date range or trust or operating balance.

Note: This export shows only bills that have been approved. It excludes bills in draft or pending approval.

  1. Go to Billing.
  2. Click the down arrow next to New bills and select New statements of account.
  3. Make the selections relevant to your export.
  4. Click Generate Statements of Account.

 

Up next

  • Split Billing: Divide a matter's bill among multiple payers.
  • Edit Bills: Download and print an individual bill.

results.name: Filter and Export Activities
results.title: Filter and Export Activities
results.body:
Firms are busy with multiple activities occurring each day across different attorneys, practice areas, and offices. To make activity management more efficient, activities can be exported out of Clio Manage as CSV or PDF files for reporting purposes.

Tip: Clio Manage offers built-in reports for billing activity and productivity, including a summary of each firm user’s time and expense history. These are great places to view financial insights about your firm to make informed and data-driven decisions. Learn more about reports here.

Filter activities

Activities can be filtered from the main Activities page or by going to a specific matter’s Activities subtab. You can filter by firm user responsible for creating the activities, whether an activity is on a bill, by matter, and by activity category. On the Activities page, you can also insert whole keywords into the Filter by keyword field to search for specific activities. This keyword search functionality will scan for whole words in the description of an activity. It will not search by activity category.

  1. Go to Activities or go to a matter’s Activities subtab.
  2. Optional: Select All, Time, or Expense in the quick filter, depending on which type of activities you want to view.
  3. Optional: Narrow by date range.
    • If you select a date range, this date range will continue to apply until you change it again, regardless of whether you refresh your browser window or exit out of Clio Manage
  4. Click Filters, select your filters, and click Apply filters.

 

Export and print activities

You can export your activities by using filters in the main Activities page or by going to a matter’s Activities subtab. You have the option to export time and expense entries together or separately. You can also export all of your activities in bulk from Clio's Exports page. Learn more here.

Note: When you export activities in CSV format, the Created at column represents the date the activity was created, and the Updated at column lists when the activity was edited. If you edit an activity but do not save your changes, this metric will not be affected.

  1. Go to Activities or go to a matter’s Activities subtab.
  2. Optional: Select All, Time, or Expense in the quick filter.
  3. Optional: Narrow by date range.
  4. Click Filters, select your filters, and click Apply filters.
  5. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Export.
  6. Choose PDF or CSV and click Export.
  7. Optional: print the export.

 

Export hard costs or client advanced costs

Client advanced costs are hard cost expenses that your firm paid on behalf of a client that your firm will later collect from the client. For accounting and compliance purposes, you may need to show the running balance of unpaid hard costs on a general ledger account as an asset. You can find and determine the client advanced cost running balance by following the steps below.

  1. Enable hard cost expenses in your settings. Learn more about how to do this here.
  2. Go to Activities and select the Expense quick filter.
  3. Update the starting and ending date ranges to view all hard costs expenses in a paid state.
    • If you are using Clio Accounting, set the ending date to the date entered for the start date in Clio Accounting.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Export.
  5. Select CSV and then click Export.
  6. Open the CSV file in Excel or another spreadsheet software. Filter out the following:
    • Under the Type column, remove soft cost entries and anything other than HardCostEntry. Only HardCostEntry entries should be remaining.
    • Under the Bill state column, remove Paid entries. Only Unpaid and blank entries should be remaining.
  7. To determine the running balance of unpaid costs, separately add up the amounts under the Billable and Non-billable columns, and then subtract the Non-billable total from the Billable total. So, the sum of all Billable amounts - the sum of all Non-billable amounts = the running balance of unpaid costs.
  8. If you are using Clio Accounting, enter this value in the opening balances field. If you are not using Clio Accounting, use this value to track the running balance of unpaid costs in your accounting solution of choice.

results.name: Filter and Export Contacts
results.title: Filter and Export Contacts
results.body:
In Clio Manage, you can filter the contacts table to a subset of your contacts and export the results as a CSV or PDF file. Filtering lets you find a contact by keyword, contact type, tag, or custom field, and exporting provides contact data you can work with outside Clio Manage. The export reflects the filters and columns you set, so the file you download matches the list on your screen.

Tip: To bring contacts into Clio Manage rather than out of it, refer to Import Contacts with Migration Templates. To keep contacts aligned between products, refer to 

Filter contacts

You can filter by whether a contact is a client, by contact tags, and by contact custom fields. The Filter by keyword field matches whole keywords.

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts.
  2. Enter the contact name in the Filter by keyword field. The results update as you type.
  3. Optional: Select All, People, or Companies to narrow the list by contact type.
  4. Optional: Click Filters to narrow the list by contact type, contact tag, or custom field.

 

Export and print contacts

An export from the contacts table includes basic contact information and any contact custom fields. Billing preferences stay out of the export. To export notes, documents, or transactions for a contact, open that contact and export from the relevant subtab instead.

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts.
  2. Optional: Select All, People, or Companies to narrow the list by contact type.
  3. Optional: Click Filters to apply specific parameters.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Export.
  5. Select the export format. Refer to the formats below.
    • CSV: Holds either every column from the contacts table or only the columns currently displayed and selected. Choose which of the two you want when you select the format.
    • PDF: Holds basic contact information.
  6. Click Export.
  7. Optional: Print the downloaded file.

results.name: View, Export, and Track Dockets
results.title: View, Export, and Track Dockets
results.body:
You can click the name of a docket from your search results to view the case details including case metadata, filings and events, and party information.

While viewing a docket, you can use the Export PDF or Download Excel icons to download the information to your computer for use outside of Clio. You can also click Track Docket to begin tracking the docket for new activity.

While viewing a docket or document, you can also expand the AI-features panel (the diamond icon) on the right to access Clio Work. The panel scopes to the docket or document you have open, and offers suggested actions such as summarizing the case, surfacing upcoming deadlines, extracting key filings, and finding related court rules. You can also type your own questions in plain language. Learn more about how to write effective prompts.

Tip: Click Sync to manually refresh the docket and pull the latest data from the court system.

 

Use Clio Work with Clio Docket

You can access Clio Work directly from any open docket or document in Clio Docket to summarize case activity, surface key details, and answer questions about what you're viewing.

From an open docket or document, click the AI icon on the right side of the screen to open a Clio Work panel. You can select one of the suggested actions, or type your own question or prompt in the text box. Learn more about how to write effective prompts.

Important: Clio Work outputs are a starting point and require review. Clio Work reads the docket as of the last sync, so click the sync icon to refresh before relying on the results. Always confirm deadlines, filings, and court rules against the docket and the court before acting on them.

 

Attach dockets to matters

You can attach a court docket to a matter from the matter dashboard in Clio Manage. Once attached, docket updates appear on the matter dashboard so you can track case activity alongside your other matter details.

  1. In Clio Manage, open the relevant matter.
  2. On the matter Dashboard, in the Docket updates section, click Attach a Docket.

  3. Search for a docket using the appropriate search parameters.

    Note: If you cannot find the docket you are looking for, click Request Docket at the bottom of the search results.

  4. Use the checkboxes to select the docket(s) from the search results. The modal displays the number of dockets selected and any applicable linking fee(s).

    Tip: You can click the docket name to open the full docket detail in a new tab, allowing you to review it before attaching.
  5. Click Attach Docket.

Once a docket is attached, the Docket updates section on the matter dashboard displays the linked case name, the last synced time, and recent case events.

  • Create and Manage Alerts: Set up alerts to receive notifications when new filings or updates are added to a docket you're tracking.
  • Search for Dockets and Documents: Run a new search to find additional dockets or documents.

results.name: Share and Export Library Documents
results.title: Share and Export Library Documents
results.body:
Once you have identified relevant authorities in Clio Library, you can share documents with colleagues, export citations to a reference manager, or download documents to upload directly to a matter in Clio Manage. Keeping research linked to the matter record ensures your team uses the same verified sources.

Share a document

You can share any document in Clio Library via email, social media, or a direct link. Share options are accessed from the document viewer toolbar.

  1. Open a document in Clio Library.
  2. In the top-right toolbar, click the share icon.
  3. Select a share method:
    • Email: Sends a link to the document. Recipients are notified from no-reply@vlex.com.
    • LinkedIn, Facebook, or Twitter: Posts a link to the document on the selected platform.

    • RefWorks, RIS: Connects to your reference manager or download a RIS file to copy relevant references information about the document.

      Note: Always review imported citations for style and accuracy before including them in a filing or memorandum.

    • Link to page: Copies a direct URL to the document.
    • ID vLex: Copies the document's unique vLex identifier for internal reference.

 

Download and save documents

You can download documents from Clio Library to save locally or upload to a matter record in Clio Manage.

Tip: Create a dedicated folder within the matter's Documents tab for research materials. This keeps verified authorities organized and accessible to everyone working on the file.

  1. Open a document in Clio Library.
  2. In the top-right toolbar, click the download icon. 
  3. Click to download in PDF or DOCX. 
  4. Save the file to your preferred location.

 

Connect research to a matter in Clio Manage

Downloaded documents can be uploaded directly to a matter record in Clio Manage, keeping your research findings connected to the file.

Note: Attaching verified research directly to the matter record can reduce the risk of using outdated or unverified authority in subsequent work. When multiple attorneys contribute to a matter, a shared document folder ensures everyone cites the same verified sources.

  1. In Clio Manage, open the relevant matter.
  2. Navigate to the Documents tab.
  3. Upload the downloaded file to the matter record.

 

Up next

With your research complete and connected to the matter, you can use Vincent AI to analyze those documents in context. See Analyze Legal Documents in Clio Work.

results.name: Import, Filter, and Export Calendars
results.title: Import, Filter, and Export Calendars
results.body:
Calendars can be exported out of Clio Manage using either CSV or ics files. You can also filter and export individual calendar entries rather than an entire calendar and print a specific calendar view.

 

Import ics calendar into Clio Manage

To import a calendar saved as an ics file, such as a holiday calendar:

  1. Go to Clio’s Imports page.
  2. Click Add.
  3. Under Import select Calendar from iCalendar (.ics).
  4. Select the destination calendar in Clio Manage.
  5. Click Choose File and find your file.
  6. Click Upload File.
  7. Wait for the import state to complete. This could take several minutes.

 

Export calendar events

You can download an ics file of your calendar or export calendar events for a specific matter as a list of events in PDF or CSV format. Using the option to download an ics file, you can subsequently add the file to a calendaring application of your choice. This export will show all future events, past events within the last 30 days, the event's date, start time, end time, summary, and description, but the export will not carry over event locations. When you download a list of calendar events for a specific matter, you have the option to filter the results by the type of calendar event or court rule and/or whether to include upcoming, past, or all events prior to the export.

Export calendar ics file Export matter events
Tip: If you need to see events in the last 6 months rather than the last 30 days, set up a Google or Office 365 sync.

To download an ics file of a calendar:

  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Click More and select Calendar feeds.
  3. For the relevant calendar, select Download [calendar_name] ics. Or, to download an ics for all of the calendars that is visible in your main calendar tab, click Download All visible calendars ics.

The ics file will be downloaded to your computer.

Tip: Enter whole keywords into the Filter by keyword field to search for specific calendar entries.

To download a list of events for a specific matter:

  1. Go to the matter’s Calendar subtab.
  2. Optional: Click Filters and/or use the Upcoming, Past, or All quick filters to select a specific subset of events.
  3. Optional: Click Columns to select or deselect the information to include for your export.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Export.
  5. Select the export format. If you select CSV, you can choose to show all columns from the table or only columns that are visible/checked.
  6. Click Export.

The file will be downloaded to your computer.

 

Print calendar views

When viewing the main Calendar tab, you can print the agenda, daily, week, work week, or month views. The printed view will show all calendar entries visible to you, excluding tasks.

  1. Go to Calendar.
  2. Select one of the following: Agenda, Day, Week, Work week, or Month.
  3. Click the More dropdown and select Print.
  4. Follow your browser’s printing directions.

results.name: Export Data From Clio Manage
results.title: Export Data From Clio Manage
results.body:
You can export your firm's data from Clio Manage for record-keeping or to migrate data to a new Clio Manage account. Exported files are downloaded in CSV format and can be used with Clio's migration templates to import data into another account.

Note: Only users with administrator permissions can export data in bulk.

Export data from Clio Manage

  1. In Clio Manage, go to the Exports page:
    • North America: https://app.clio.com/export
    • Canada: https://ca.app.clio.com/export
  2. Click Excel ready CSV next to each of the following data types you want to export:
    • Calendar entries
    • Communications
    • Contact notes
    • Contact related matters
    • Contacts
    • Expense entries
    • Matter notes
    • Matters
    • Tasks
    • Time entries
  3. To export outstanding balances, go to Reports, click Reports, then click Accounts receivable. Set the output format to CSV and click Generate Report.

 

Migrate data to a new Clio Manage account

If you are migrating data from one Clio Manage account to another, use the exported CSV files with Clio's migration templates to import data into the new account.

  1. Export your data from the original Clio Manage account following the steps above. For trust balances, generate the trust management report before exporting.
  2. Move the data from the exported CSV files into the appropriate migration templates.
  3. Import the completed templates into the new Clio Manage account. See Get Started with Migration Templates for import instructions.

You can filter matters in Clio Manage for reporting purposes and also export specific matter details for use outside of Clio Manage.

 

Filter matters

When filtering matters in Clio Manage, you can filter by contact, responsible or originating attorney, matter notifications, billable status, matter permissions groups, grants, whether evergreen trust is enabled or disabled, practice area, matter status, matter tag, and more.

 

Tip: You can select the number of matters per page to display in your matter table by selecting one of the options at the bottom of the matter table.

 To filter matters:

  1. Go to Matters.

When filters are applied, a checkmark appears next to the Filters button. To clear it, click Filters > Clear filters.

 

Export matter details

When exporting matters from the main Matters tab, the export will only include the data that you entered in the matter form when the matter was created or edited. If you need to export information such as activities or transactions related to a matter, you can do so from that particular subtab of the matter. To export the matter form details for matters.

The data from all matters for the applied filters will be exported, not just the page you are viewing.

results.name: Legal Aid US: Grants Dashboards, Exports, and Reports
results.title: Legal Aid US: Grants Dashboards, Exports, and Reports
results.body:
View dashboards and metrics 

There are three different dashboards and an organization timeline to help you keep track of how time is spent on matters and grants:

Personal Dashboard:

This dashboard shows a high-level overview of your agenda, how you are spending your time, and financial metrics. A comprehensive description of the dashboard is provided here. When grant information is tracked it also includes information about how you are spending your time in relation to grants and their associated matters.

  • Time allocation: This section shows your time entries in hours for the specified timeframe. If grants are associated with any time entries, they are listed in this section.
    • You can use the Filter to display information about the proportion of time allocated to each grant in hours, as a percentage, or both.
    • You can click Review activities for any listed grant to view a table of the transactions associated with that grant.
    • You can select a date range and relevant filters to view specific information and export the data using Export CSV.

Organization Dashboard:

Note: The primary subscriber or users with administrator permissions can view this dashboard.

This dashboard shows a high-level overview of how firm members are spending their time and what their billing practices are. A comprehensive description of the dashboard is provided here. When grant information is tracked, it also includes information about how firm members are spending their time in relation to grants and on matters associated with grants.

  • Time allocation: This section shows time entries for the specified timeframe across firm users.
    • You can use the Filter to display information about the proportion of time allocated to each grant in hours, as a percentage, or both.
    • You can click Review activities for any listed grant to view a table of the transactions associated with that grant.
    • You can select a date range and relevant filters to view specific information and export the data using Export CSV.

Organization Feed:

This feed shows a timeline of all organization-wide activity in the account. A comprehensive description of the feed is provided here. Relevant to grants, the feed provides information related to grant spend down via salaries, such as updates to grant allocations, changes to salary amounts, and the spend down amounts.

Matter Dashboard:

This dashboard provides an overview of matter information. A comprehensive description of the feed is provided here. When you add a grant to a matter, that matter's dashboard will show a new section for grants associated with the matter.

 

Generate a matters and grants report

If you use grants at your firm, you can generate a Matters & grants report which offers information similar to a matter report but with additional options to filter by grant, matter custom fields, and client custom fields.

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. In the list of categories, select Matters.
  3. Click Matters & grants.
  4. Make your selections.
  5. Click Generate report.

 

Export matters with associated grants

In the main Matters tab, you can select columns and specify filters relevant to a particular export you may need to track a specific deliverable, including cases closed under a specific grant. When adding a grant to a matter, if you check the box for Use this grant for case reporting, the grant will appear in the Grants column and in the export.

Tip: When selecting your filters and columns, you also have the option to select custom fields. These custom fields will appear in your export, allowing you to report on them.

  1. Go to Matters.
  2. Click Columns, check the box for Grants, and then click Update columns.
  3. Select Filters to sort data by specific filters, including specific grants or custom fields, and then click Apply filters.
  4. Optional: In the search box, use a keyword search to filter your matters.
  5. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.

 

Export activities with associated grants

In the main Activities tab, you can select columns and specify filters relevant to a particular export you may need to track a specific deliverable. To export grant information from the Activities tab:

  1. Go to Activities.
  2. Click Columns, check the boxes for Grant and Matter, and then click Update columns.
  3. Select Filters to sort data by specific filters, including specific grants, and then click Apply filters.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.

 

Export grants

In the Grants tab, you can export your organization's grants to get an understanding of how much of a spend down there has been from the grants. The data will be exported in CSV format.

  1. Go to Grants.
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.
Note: All active and archived grants will be exported regardless of the subtab you selected.

 

Export grant transactions

You can export the transactions associated with a grant to get an understanding of the detailed financials of a specific grant. The data will be exported in CSV format and will show grant spend down in your firm.

  1. Go to Grants.
  2. Select the name of a grant to view its transactions.

  3. Optional: You can add or remove columns to include or exclude in the export by clicking Columns, selecting and/or deselecting column fields, and clicking Update columns.

    Note: You can select a time period to filter the list of transactions in the table, but the export will include all transactions for a grant regardless of the time period you selected.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the table and click Export.
  5. Choose between exporting Available columns, which will include all available columns even if you previously deselected them, or Visible columns only to include only those columns you appearing in the table view.
  6. Click Export.

results.title: QuickBooks Desktop and Clio
results.body:
QuickBooks desktop is a desktop-based accounting software. You can export payment and trust transactions and bills from Clio to QuickBooks Desktop for accounting purposes.

Tip: Check out the QuickBooks Community Knowledge Base for more information about using QuickBooks, including how to resolve specific error codes.

Set up QuickBooks Desktop

Since QuickBooks Desktop does not integrate directly with Clio, the setup process is done by setting up a Chart of Accounts in QuickBooks Desktop and then mapping Clio IIF exports to QuickBooks ledger accounts. Once this is done, you can begin exporting transactions and bills out of Clio and importing them into QuickBooks Desktop.

Important: Changing the default settings is not recommended unless you are very familiar with QuickBooks Desktop and accounting.
  1. In Clio Manage, go to Accounts > Export transactions.
  2. Under Export Format, click QuickBooks Export Options.
  3. Optional: Change which accounts you want Clio to use with exports.
  4. Click Update QuickBooks Export Options.
  5. To reset the options to default mappings, delete the fields and then click Update QuickBooks Export Options.

 

Export account transactions

You can export account transactions in Clio in either QuickBooks IIF or QuickBooks CSV format. Once exported, go into your QuickBooks Desktop account, and import the file.

  1. Go to Accounts > Export transactions.
  2. Select the bank account you want to export transactions for.
  3. Select the date range for transactions.
  4. Select the QuickBooks export format.
  5. Click Export Transactions.
  6. Import the file into QuickBooks Desktop.

 

Export bills

You can export account transactions in Clio in PDF or CSV format, or as IIF files. Once exported, go into your QuickBooks Desktop account, and import the file.

PDF or CSV IIF
  1. Go to Billing.
  2. Optional: Select the appropriate bill state.
  3. Select the bills you want to export.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Export.
  5. Select the output format.
  6. Click Export.
  7. Import the file into QuickBooks Desktop.
  1. Go to Clio's export page.
  2. Click QuickBooks CSV & IIF next to Bank Transactions or Bills.
  3. Select the relevant export parameters.
  4. Under Format, select Quickbooks IIF.
  5. Click Export Transactions or Export Bills.

 

Perform trust account reconciliation

Tip: Clio offers full trust account reconciliation right in Clio Manage. Learn more here.

If you are performing trust account reconciliation in QuickBooks Desktop, you can do so by exporting trust transactions from Clio to QuickBooks Desktop, running the trust ledger report in Clio, and then matching transactions in QuickBooks Desktop.

  1. Follow the steps above in Export account transactions to export trust transactions and then import them into QuickBooks Desktop.
  2. In Clio Manage, go to Reports > Reports.
  3. Click Client under Categories.
  4. Select the Trust ledger report.
  5. Choose your parameters
  6. Select Generate report.
  7. Go to QuickBooks Desktop and compare the amounts.

results.body:
This article explains what data can be migrated from your current practice management software and how to export the data from that software. Software applications starting with the letters A and B are listed below.

Abacus

What can I migrate? How do I migrate my data?
  • Contacts
  • Matters 
  • Contact notes
  • Matter notes
  • Related Contacts
  • Tasks
  • Calendar Events
  • Email Communications
Note: The following steps apply to exporting your contacts, matters, and notes. To export other data types, such as calendar events or tasks, follow the instructions in the Abacus help center.

Before migrating your data, ensure all users are logged out of AbacusLaw, Abacus Accounting, MessageSlips, and Microsoft Outlook. If you need to force all users out, go to File > Setup > Scheduled Shutdown. Under the Immediate shutdown section, click Shutdown Now.

Option 1: Back up your data

Important: If your firm uses a PostgreSQL server for Abacus, standard backup methods will not be sufficient for a complete data export. The DATA01 folder will not contain up-to-date data, and this backup option will not work. You can identify your server type by going to Help > About Abacus. For PostgreSQL servers, use one of the other export options below.

  1. Log in to Abacus.
  2. Click File.
  3. Select Utilities > Backup > Backup.
  4. Check that the Destination is set to your preferred location.
  5. Click Backup. A backup file in the form of LAW_XXX.zip will be created and stored in the selected directory. The "X" refers to the backup number.

 

Option 2: Export your data

  1. In Abacus, go to File > Reports.
  2. Select one of the following: Names, Calendar, Matters, Matter Notes, or Name Notes.
  3. Click New Report.
  4. Enter a new name for the report (e.g., Clio Contact Export) and click OK.
  5. In the upper left of the screen, click Add.
  6. Click Run.
  7. Click Comma Delimited.
  8. Click Ok and then save the file.
  9. Search for law9.adt  or law9.dbf in the Abacus folder on your computer.

 

Option 3: Export from a PostgreSQL server

If you have a PostgreSQL server, you will need to use a different export method.

  1. Use the export feature in Abacus Accounting.
  2. In Abacus Law, select File > Export and follow the instructions on the web page.
  3. You can also contact Abacus directly to request an export for a fee.

  1. Log in to your database as an Administrator or a Manager level Act! user.

  3. Click Browse..., then find the location where you will save the backup.
  4. Give the file a new name (if desired), and then click Save.
  5. Uncheck Include Attachments. These are not included in the migration.
  6. Choose whether you want to password-protect the database backup file.
  7. Click OK to begin backing up the items into a .ZIP file.

  1. Open SQL Server Management Studio Express and connect to the SQL server.

  9. On the Locate Database Files window, select the folder where you want the backup file to go. By default, it is ..\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL.1\MSSQL\Backup.

      • If your organization uses divisions, data from all divisions is included in the export.
      • If your organization uses person accounts and you are exporting accounts, all account fields are included in the account data.
      • If your organization uses person accounts and you are exporting contacts, person account records are included in the contact data. However, the contact data only includes the fields shared by contacts and person accounts.

Database Backup

Note: Clio requires only the SQL database backup, which uses the default naming convention "TimeMattersAutomatedBackup[Day].bak". Find this file in the default backup location for the Microsoft SQL Server. Time Matters SQL database backups are stored in a different location than Time Matters document and email file backups, which are backed up to the Server. The default location for SQL backup data is C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL.XX\MSSQL\Backup or C:\Program Files(x86)\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL.XX\MSSQL\Backup.

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Backup Time Matters Data.

  5. Check the box next to Skip files in the Documents and Documents Index Directories.
  6. Check the box next to Skip backing up of email attachments.
  7. To keep a non-default Shared Files Backup location for future backups, check the box next to Remember this destination for future backups.

Step 1: Contact TrialWorks to request a backup of the TrialWorks database.

Step 2: Follow these steps to access the data in your backup:

  1. Open SQL Server Management Studio Express and connect to the SQL server.
  2. Expand Databases.
  3. Right-click on the database you want to back up, and then select Tasks > Back up (this is not available for version 2018/2019).

  5. Select Full for the Backup Type.
  6. Click Remove to remove the default/last backup file name.
  7. Click Add to open the Select Backup Destination window.
  8. Click [...] next to the File Name field.
  9. On the Locate Database Files window, select the folder where you want the backup file to go. By default, it is ..\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL.1\MSSQL\Backup.

  11. Click OK to close the Locate Database Files window.
  12. Click OK to close the Select Backup Destination window.

There are two options for backing up Juris data. See the steps below for more information.

  • Juris Management Console Backup
  • Backing up Juris using SQL Server management Studio

Note: All users will need to be logged out of Juris for the backup.

Option 1: Juris Management Console Backup

Juris backups include Juris Suite time and expense entries that have been synchronized with the server, as indicated with an entry key within the grid. Time and expense entries stored only in the local cache file (not synchronized) are not included in the backup. Additionally, backing up via Juris Management Console also shrinks the LDF file upon completion. Follow these steps to create a backup using the Juris Management Console (JMC):

  1. Verify that all users have closed Juris.
  2. Click the Start button on the Windows Taskbar.
  3. Select Programs > Juris > Administrative Tools > Juris Management Console to the open the Juris Management Console window.
  4. Double-click Juris Management Console to expand the folder in the Juris Console list.
  5. Double-click [Your Firms Name] Data to expand the folder.
  6. Right-click the Database folder and select All Tasks and then Backup to open the Juris Backup wizard.
  7. Click the Right Arrow button once.
  8. Select New Backup from the Backup Device list.
  9. Enter the Name of your backup in the Name field. For example you can enter Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or End of year as the name of your backup file.
  10. Click to check the File radial box to enter a destination path for saving your backup.
  11. Click the ellipsis button to open the Browse for location of Backup file window.
  12. Select the folder you want to save your backup to. The file path needs to reside on the server and not on the local workstation.
  13. Click OK to return to the Add New Backup Device window.
  14. Enter \[Name of your backup].bak at the end of the destination path in the File field. The [Name of your backup] is the same name as you entered for step 9.
  15. Click OK.
  16. Click the Right Arrow button once.
  17. Click the Right Arrow button to open the Backup Confirmation window and do not change the Media Name field. The Media Name field is populated from the Windows System Clock.
  18. Click Finish to backup Juris.
  19. Click the X to close the Juris Management Console.

 

Option 2: Backing up Juris using SQL Server management Studio

Follow these steps to backup your Juris data using the SQL Server Management Studio:

  1. Verify that all users have closed the Juris program.
  2. Place Juris in Maintenance or Backup mode depending on reason for backup.
  3. Click Start and select Programs > Microsoft SQL Server > SQL Server Management Studio to the open the Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio window.
  4. Log in with your credentials.
  5. Click next to Databases to expand it.
  6. Right-click Juris [ your client code ] and select Tasks, and then Back Up... to open the Back Up Database - Juris[ your client code ]window.
  7. Select Full from the Backup type: dropdown list.
  8. Enter the[ Name of your backup ] in the Name field.
  9. Click Add... to open the Select Backup Destination window.
  10. Click the ellipsis button to the right of the File name field to open the Locate Database Files window.
  11. Click to select the folder where you want to save your backup.
  12. Enter the[ Name of your backup ].bak in the File name field and click OK.
  13. Click OK on the Select Backup Destination window.
  14. Click OK on the Back Up Database - Juris [ your client code ] window to start the backup.
  15. Click OK on the Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio The backup of database 'Juris[ your client code ]' completed successfully window.
  16. Right-click JBills[ your client code ] and select Tasks, and then Back Up... to open the Back Up Database - JBills[ your client code ] window.
  17. Select Full from the Backup type dropdown list.
  18. Enter the [ name of your backup ] in the Name field. Use the same Backup set Name that you used for Juris[ your client code ]to append the JBills database backup to the Juris database backup.
  19. Click Add... to open the Select Backup Destination window.
  20. Click the ellipsis button to the right of the File name field to open the Locate Database Files window.
  21. Click to select the folder where you want to save your backup. Use the same destination file that you used forJuris[ your client code ]to append the JBills database backup to the Juris database backup.
  22. Enter the name of your backup in the File name field and click OK. Use the same File name that you used forJuris[ your client code ]to append the JBills database backup to the Juris database backup.
  23. Click OK on the Select Backup Destination window.
  24. Click OK on the Back Up Database - JBills[ your client code ] window to start the backup.
  25. Click OK on the Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio The backup of database 'JBills[ your client code ]' completed successfully window.
  26. Close Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio.

results.name: Clio Manage Data Migration Overview
results.title: Clio Manage Data Migration Overview
results.body:
Clio Manage supports data migration from your previous software or client management system. You can transfer your firm's existing contacts, matters, activities, and other records into your new account. This article covers what data can and cannot be migrated, and what you can expect from the data migration process.

Note: Migrations can be completed independently using Clio's self-serve tools and migration templates, or with the assistance of Clio's migrations team. If your firm has complex data or you would prefer hands-on support, a migrations team member can walk you through the export process and manage the import on your behalf. To request assisted migration, contact Clio Support. 

Data that can be migrated

The following data types can be migrated to Clio Manage during a standard migration.

Note: If your Clio Manage account includes preconfigured custom fields or matter templates for specific practice areas, review Preconfigured Accounts before beginning your migration. Preconfigured settings may affect how imported data is mapped.

  • Contacts
  • Matters
  • Related contacts
  • Tasks
  • Notes
  • Calendar events
  • Emails
  • Phone logs
  • Unbilled activities (time entries only)
  • Accounts receivable balances (a single line item per matter, representing the summative balance at the time of export)
  • Trust balances (a single line item per matter or contact, representing the balance at the time of export)
  • Documents (subject to scoping and additional fees based on volume)

 

Data that cannot be migrated

The following data types cannot be migrated to Clio Manage.

  • Accounting and financial history, including trust account transactions, trust account requests, trust account payments, operating account transactions, invoices, billed time entries, accounts receivable ledgers, bill payments, and historical bills
  • Billable rates (user rate, client rate, and matter rate)
  • Reports
  • User permissions
  • Settings

 

Understand the migration process

A standard migration follows four steps. The time required at each step depends on the size and complexity of your data.

Step 1: Export your data

Export your data from your previous practice management software. Find export instructions for your previous software in the Software Migration Guides.

Important: Once you export data from your previous system, stop using that system immediately. Any data entered after the export will not be captured in Clio Manage and must be transferred manually.

 

Step 2: Prepare and submit your data

If you are sending your data to Clio's migrations team, review and clean it to ensure accurate import. See Prepare Data for Migration for detailed preparation steps, including what to review for each data type and how to manage your firm during the transition period.

 

Step 3: Data processing

Once Clio's migrations team receives your data export, they convert it into a format compatible with Clio Manage. Processing time varies depending on the size and complexity of your data. A team member will contact you with a timeline.

 

Step 4: Import and review

Clio imports the processed data into your Clio Manage account. Once the import is complete, review your data for accuracy and contact the migrations team immediately if any corrections are needed.

Important: Do not modify imported data until you have confirmed it is accurate. Modifications can prevent the import from being reverted if corrections are needed.

 

Up next

Before exporting your data, review Prepare Data for Migration for critical steps to complete in your previous system and guidance on managing your firm during the transition period.

results.body:
In Clio Manage, the Bill Timeline is designed to help your firm answer client billing questions by providing a log of any bill events and communications. You can also access past versions of sent bills. For more detailed information, you can download a PDF of a historical version or export a CSV of the timeline information.

View bill timeline

Once a bill is approved, the timeline will show any event that results in a state change, payments made, upcoming autocharge events, edits to activities or expenses made when viewing, accrued interest, discounts, credit notes, write offs, and communications. You can download previous and current trust requests and bills, view communication and export the timeline. 

Note: If an action includes multiple events (such as approving and applying trust), each event will share the same timestamp on the bill timeline.

  1. Go to the Billing tab or the Bills subtab of a matter or client.
  2. Click the Bill ID number to view the bill.
  3. Scroll down to Bill Timeline to view the timeline of bill-related events log including its internal edits, changes in its state (e.g., from a bill in draft to an approved bill, whether it was downloaded by a firm user and/or sent via email or text, payments made, interest applied, and discounts applied. For bill sent events and bill download events (by firm users), Clio Manage logs the event details and saves a historical version of the bill for the event.
    • Download bill: Click Download bill to download and view what the bill looked like at the time of the logged event.
    • View email log: Click View email log to view more details of the email communication.
    • View client portal: Click View client portal to view more details of the client portal communication.
    • View text log: Click View text log to view more details of the text communication.

 

Export bill timeline

You can export a bill timeline in CSV format when viewing a bill or trust request. The export includes the date and time of the event and a description that includes the name of the user and details of the event.

To export a bill timeline:

  1. Go to the Billing tab or the Bills subtab of a matter or client.
  2. Click the Bill ID number to view the bill.
  3. Scroll down, under Bill Timeline click Export.

results.name: View Reconciliation Reports
results.title: View Reconciliation Reports
results.body:
Every completed trust account reconciliation produces a report for that reconciliation period. The report is your audit-ready record of the period: it shows the balances you reconciled to, every transaction you matched, and the effect on each client's ledger. You can view the report in Clio Manage or export it as a PDF to use outside Clio.

Note: If your plan includes Clio Accounting, view your reconciliation reports in Clio Accounting instead. See Clio Accounting: Operating and Trust Reconciliation.

What a reconciliation report includes

Each report covers one reconciliation period and is available in three tabs:

  • Reconciliation summary: The ledger and bank account balances for the period, and the difference between them.
  • Transaction details: The transactions for the reconciliation period, broken out as funds in, funds out, bank interest, bank charges, and adjustments. Both cleared and uncleared transactions are included.
  • Client ledger details: The effect of the period's transactions on each client's trust ledger.

Reconciliation reports can be accessed in Clio Manage for 10 years, so you keep a full history for audit and compliance purposes.

 

View a reconciliation report

  1. Go to Accounts.
  2. Click the relevant trust account name.
  3. Select the Reconciliations subtab.
  4. Click View report for the relevant reconciliation.
  5. Use the three tabs to view the reconciliation summary, transaction details, and client ledger details.

 

Export a reconciliation report

Export the report when you need a copy outside Clio Manage, such as for a regulator, an auditor, or your bookkeeper.

  1. Open the reconciliation report using the steps above.
  2. Click Export to download a PDF file of the report.
Tip: The export includes all three tabs, so you do not need to export each one separately.

Up next

  • Void or Delete a Reconciliation: Void a completed reconciliation or delete one that is still in progress.
  • Trust Reconciliation in Clio: Start a reconciliation and match transactions.

results.title: Navigate Clio Manage
results.body:
Clio Manage is a practice management software where you can manage your law firm clients, cases, files, billing, payments, and much more. After signing up for Clio Manage, you can begin setting up your account. Take a look at the resources below to learn more about navigating the Clio Manage interface.

Tip: Learn more about setting up Clio Manage here.

Header

Across the top of your Clio Manage interface is your home for all quick access items. From your header you can search using the global search bar, view recently viewed contacts and matters, start a billing timer, and create new assets. The header will also show you your notifications, which can be managed in your settings.

 

Side navigation bar

Use the navigation bar to access case-specific files and resources for your account. When you click each tab, you will see a header with subtabs for navigating actions in the section and a table for navigating and manipulating data. Clio Manage contains the following tabs:

Dashboard

Personal Dashboard

Firm Dashboard, Organization Dashboard

Firm Feed

Personal Dashboard

The Personal Dashboard gives you a snapshot of pertinent information related to your overall personal and specific matters and includes the following:

  • Today's Agenda: This section shows your tasks that are due today and your calendar events for the day.
  • Hourly Metrics: This section shows your target billable time compared to the actual billable time that you logged. Non-billable time will not appear as part of this metric. You can set your personal performance targets for this metric in your settings. See the "Set up personal performance target" section here to learn more.
  • Billing Metrics for Firm: This section shows the number of bills and value amount totals that you have in each bill state. You can only view this section if you are an administrator or if you have billing and reports permissions, and if your billing rate visibility is not restricted.
  • Financial Metrics: This section shows billed and unbilled time entered in Clio for the fiscal year, plotted relative to the annual performance targets. The calculations in each graph are based on a 260-day year to account for weekends. You can only view this section if you are an administrator or if you have billing and reports permissions, and if your billing rate visibility is not restricted.
  • Detailed Annual Report: This report shows a visual of your personal performance metrics. It displays the target billable time you aimed to reach by the end of the year compared to the actual billable time you logged for the year. You can only view this section if you are an administrator or if you have billing and reports permissions, and if your billing rate visibility is not restricted. Learn more here.
Firm Dashboard

The Firm Dashboard offers managers, administrators, and users with reporting permissions insights into the utilization, realization, and collection metrics of their firms. It presents data by your desired year and can be adjusted with the date selector at the top of the page. This dashboard calculates all metrics based on the date of an activity, not the date of a payment or bill. 

  • Utilization: The utilization rate is a measure of productivity and shows how much of the day is spent doing billable work in comparison to the available hours in a day (Clio uses an eight-hour available work day). It is calculated as the billable hours worked divided by the available working hours (in the number of days in a month). Each user's working days are defined by the values set for their personal performance target.
  • Realization: The realization rate is a measure of value efficiency and shows the amount of billable work recorded that is actually put on a bill, excluding any discounts. It is calculated as the total number of billed hours subtracted by the discounted hours and then divided by the total number of billable hours worked.
  • Collection: The collection rate shows how much of the firm's billed work clients have paid for. It is calculated as the total amount of hours collected divided by the total number of non-discounted hours billed.
Firm Feed

The firm feed allows you to monitor account activity and events for the firm (e.g., creating matters and contacts, recording payments, updating bills, creating, editing, and deleting time and expense entries, changing user permissions, uploading documents, and much more). Filters help narrow the view by user, type, and whether an activity or event was deleted or exported. 

Important: The Firm Feed is only visible to users with the Administrator role by default. To grant other users access, create a custom role, enable the View account firm feed permission in Firm Settings, and assign that role to them.

Available Type filters include the following:

  • Calendar: Filter by calendar entries, entry types, and membership types.
  • Tasks: Filter by task types.
  • Matter: Filter by bills, matter stages, trust requests, notes, permissions, and protected funds.
  • Contacts: Filter by people, companies, contact notes, client bills, and trust requests.
  • Clio for Co-Counsel: Filter by co-counsel permissions.
  • Activities: Filter by time entries, expense entries, and hard or soft costs. The row for a newly created Time Entry will display the start time when the timer is used. Look for the line that states [user name] created Time Entry, about [time] ago. The timestamp on the right will display the exact date and time the timer was started. You can also track updates to the entry, which appear as new rows when you select a matter or change the activity description.

  • Exports: Filter to view a log of export events for matter list exports, contact list exports, and activity list exports. Admin exports performed through the Admin Export Page are not logged in the Firm Feed.

    Note: The firm feed will only include export events that occur after Jan. 15, 2025.
  • Bills: Filter by payments and interest.
  • Online Payments: Filter by merchant account mapping and Clio Payments.
  • Accounts: Filter by refunds, trust request payments, and refunds.
  • Communication: Filter by conversations, messages, emails, and phone calls.
  • Documents: Filter by document versions and signature requests.
  • Settings: Filter by payment profiles, users, recovery events, invitations, and logins.
  • Personal injury: Filter by personal injury settings, damages, and liens.

  • Role membership: Filter by user permission changes.

    Note: The firm feed will only include permission change events that occur after Apr. 8, 2025.

If your firm uses multiple currencies, you can use the currency dropdown in the Personal Dashboard and Firm Dashboard to view the metrics for currencies other than the firm’s default currency.

Calendar

In this tab, you can navigate how you view your calendars, change months, and change date views. You can also add new calendar events, as well as share and modify calendar preferences. Learn more about calendars here.

Tasks

In this tab, you can view tasks depending on whether they are outstanding or completed tasks, search by date range, and filter results further. You can also manage task types, task lists, task feeds, and create new tasks. Learn more about tasks here.

Matters

In this tab, you can view matters by matter status (open, pending, closed), search through matters quickly and easily with a keyword search, add or remove columns, filter the table view, and add new matters. Learn more about matters here.

Contacts

In this tab, you can view contacts by contact type (person or company contacts), search through contacts quickly and easily with a keyword search, add or remove columns, filter the table view, and add new contacts. Learn more about contacts here.

Activities

In this tab, you can view activities by time or expense entries, sort by date range, search through activities quickly and easily with a keyword search, add or remove columns, and filter the table view. You can also manage activity categories and add new time and expense entries. Learn more about activities here.

Billing

In this tab, you can view current or outstanding bills and further differentiate bills by bill state, search through bills quickly and easily with a bill ID search, add or remove columns, and filter the table view. You can also record payments on bills and generate new bills. Learn more about bills here.

Online payments

In this tab, you can view a transaction history for clients by all clients, authorized transactions, completed transactions, and failed transactions. You can also view existing payment plans by all plans, active plans, stopped plans, and completed plans for which bills have been fully paid, and create new payment plans and new transaction charges. Learn more about payments here.

Accounts

In this tab, you can view your connected bank accounts, export account information, create new bank accounts, add or remove columns, and filter the table view. Learn more about bank accounts here.

Documents

In this tab, you can view documents stored in Clio Manage and documents from connected third-party document applications by both files and folders or only files. You can also search through documents quickly and easily with a keyword search, add or remove columns, filter the table view, upload new documents, and connect Clio's cloud-based document management application, Clio Drive. Learn more about documents here and Clio Drive here.

E-filings

In this tab, firms in Texas or Georgia who enable Clio File can view electronic filings by submission status or e-filing status. You can also create new filings, edit drafts, and cancel submissions. To learn more about e-filing with Clio, see Clio File: E-File and E-Serve Documents.

Communications

In this tab, you will find an inbox-style display that allows you to add new communications, reply to messages, and navigate through existing conversations and communication logs. You can quickly click through different communication channels and use subtabs to sort data by owner or type. Within each communication channel, you can sort by date or alphabetically, as well as filter and search using keywords. Learn more about communications here.

Reports

Get unique insights into all aspects of how your firm is performing. Reports can be filtered by categories, with details of what will be pulled on screen. Learn more about reports here.

App Integrations

  • Home: The Clio App directory is a quick way to explore the apps available to make your Clio account unique to your needs. Learn more about integrations here.
  • Search: Want to make your Clio experience even better? Do a keyword search for what you are looking for and add the integration that is right for you.
  • My Integrations: Click this tab to find a list of your active integrations.

Settings

In this tab, you can set up, enable, and disable various Clio Manage settings. Learn more here.

 

Resource center

  • Offers: Curious about Clio product offers and promotions? Check out this section in your side panel for more details on what Clio is offering right now. 
  • Help Center: The Help Center is Clio's knowledge base for getting answers to your product and workflow questions. Quickly and easily access a breadth of learning materials right from this side panel.
  • Law Community: The Law Community is a place for Clio customers to connect with each other, offer support, answer questions, and help each other be more successful. This is a dedicated place to meet other innovative and passionate legal professionals like yourself. 

Important: If you cannot log in to the Law Community using your Clio credentials, sign up for your community account using the create an account option located on the login window. The following users will not be able to access the community using their Clio credentials and should use the create an account option when logging in for the first time.

  • Accounts that are less than two weeks old.
  • Customers who are still in trial.
  • Customers with accounts hosted on our European or Canadian servers.
  • Customers who use the mobile two-factor push notification feature.

results.name: Prepare Data For Migration
results.title: Prepare Data For Migration
results.body:
Reviewing and cleaning your data before migration ensures that records transfer accurately into Clio Manage. Clio's migrations team does not clean or modify your data. Any errors or duplicates in your previous system will carry over on import.

Important: Set a firm-wide cut-off time before your scheduled export. Once you export data from your previous system, stop using it immediately. Any data entered after the export will not be captured in Clio Manage. You will need to manually transfer the data entered after the export. Do not enable contact or calendar syncs, or any Clio integrations, until your migration is complete.

Contacts

Verify that data appears in the correct column before exporting. Phone numbers should not appear in email fields, and company names should not appear in name fields. Check a sample of records, including the first and last rows, to confirm data is correctly placed. Include the following fields.

  • First name
  • Last name
  • Company name (required for company contacts)

 

Matters

Matters without a description will be assigned a placeholder description on import. Matters without an assigned client will be assigned to an unknown client. Include the following fields.

  • Matter status (Open, Pending, or Closed)
  • Matter custom number
  • Matter description
  • Client

 

Activities

Time entries without an assigned user will not import. If you need to import data for a user who will not be added to the Clio account, contact your migrations representative. Include the following fields.

  • Date
  • Quantity
  • Rate
  • User

 

Calendar events

Verify that your calendar events have exported correctly by checking a sample of past and future events, including court dates and scheduled meetings. Include the following fields.

  • Calendar summary
  • Start date and start time
  • End date and end time
  • Destination or user calendar

 

Contact and matter notes

Contact notes will not import without a contact or company name. Matter notes will not import without a matter number. Include the following fields.

Contact notes

Date, subject, note description, and first name, last name, or company name.

Matter notes

Date, subject, note description, and matter number.

 

Related contacts

Each related contact requires a matter. Include the following fields.

  • Matter
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Company name

 

Tasks

Tasks without an assigned user will not import. If your tasks do not have an assigned user, remove them from the data set or confirm with your migrations representative. Include the following fields.

  • Status (Pending, In-Progress, or Complete)
  • Task name
  • Due date
  • Assigned user

 

Accounts receivable balances

Verify that the balances exported from your previous system are correct before submitting. If your export includes multiple columns with outstanding amounts, identify which amount should be imported and confirm this with your migrations representative. Include the following fields.

  • Balance
  • User
  • Date

 

Manage the firm during the transition period

Data processing typically takes several business days, depending on the size and complexity of your data. During this period, your firm will need to continue recording time and expenses in Clio Manage. Records added during the transition period will need to be reconciled after migration is complete.

Use one of the following methods to track activities during the transition period.

Method 1: Placeholder matter

Create a temporary matter to record time entries while waiting for the migration to complete. Once migration is confirmed accurate, an administrator can move the time entries in bulk to their respective matters.

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts.
  2. Create a new company contact using your firm's name.
  3. Create a new matter for this contact and enter Placeholder - Migrations as the matter description.
  4. Add time entries to this matter, using the Description field to specify which matter each entry belongs to.
  5. Once migration is complete and data accuracy is confirmed, move the time entries in bulk to their respective matters.

 

Method 2: Import templates

You can track activities and matter notes using Clio's migration import templates, then upload the completed spreadsheet into Clio Manage and link entries to their respective matters after migration. See Get Started with Migration Templates for template downloads and import instructions.

Note: Generate bills for any outstanding time and expense entries in your previous software before the cut-off date to obtain the most current outstanding balances. Apply credits and trust payments to outstanding bills before exporting, as credits and trust balances will not be migrated. Export any historical banking and trust reports you want to retain as reference documents and upload them to Clio Manage under the Documents tab.

 

Up Next

Once migration is complete, review Manage Clio Manage Data After Migration for steps to verify your imported data and process outstanding accounts receivable balances.

results.name: Legal Aid US: Matters
results.title: Legal Aid US: Matters
results.body:
Once you have set up your funding sources and grants, your Legal Aid organization can associate grants to matters, reorder grants, set a primary grant for each matter, select grants for reports and exports, and remove grants from matters.

Tip: Learn more about creating matters here.

Add grants to matters

You can add a grant to a matter when creating a new matter or when editing an existing matter. There is no limit to the number of grants that can be added to a matter.

Tip: Click Recents in the Clio Manage header to see a list of matters you recently viewed.
  1. Create a new matter or go to an existing matter and click Edit matter.
  2. Go to the Grants section.
  3. Next to Primary grant, start typing the grant name or use the down arrow to display a list of grants. Select the appropriate grant from the list.
  4. Optional: Check the box for Use this grant for case reporting to track which grants should be counted towards reporting. This will impact whether the grant appears in the matter's dashboard and in data exports.
  5. Optional: Click Add a grant to add additional grants.
  6. Click Save matter.

 

Reorder grants and set primary grant

Once you have added grants to matters, you can change the order that they appear on matters and select the primary grant for each matter by dragging and dropping grants before or after other grants. The grant placed in the top position will be the primary grant.

  1. Go to a matter and click Edit matter.
  2. Under the Grants section, click and hold the horizontal three-line icon associated with a grant to drag it above or below another grant.
  3. Repeat step 2 until you are satisfied with the order of your grants.
  4. Click Save matter.

 

Select grants for case reporting

Once you have added grants to matters, you can choose which of the grants should count toward reporting. The selected grants will appear in case reports and data exports. 

  1. Go to a matter and click Edit matter.
  2. Under the Grants section, check the box next to Use this grant for case reporting for any grant that you want to use in reports and exports.
  3. Click Save matter.

 

Remove grants from matters

Once applied to matters, you can remove grants from matters and replace them with new ones. 

Important: You cannot remove a grant from a matter if there are attached time or expense activities. To remove the grant, delete the time and expense activities first. 
  1. Go to a matter and click Edit matter.
  2. Under the Grants section, click the X beside the grant's name.
  3. Click Save matter.

results.name: Record and Manage Phone Logs
results.title: Record and Manage Phone Logs
results.body:
In Clio Manage, you can store records of phone calls in the main Communications tab and the Communications subtabs for a contact and a matter. You can also add time to phone logs and capture phone conversations as billable or non-billable.

Note: All firm users can access phone logs. If you need to restrict a phone log from other firm users, you can set matter permissions, which will carry over to matter communications.

Add phone logs

You can add a new phone log from the main Communications tab, from the matter or contact Communications subtab, or from the global Create new button. If a matter is not selected when adding a new phone log, the phone log will be stored in the contact’s record.

  1. Click Create new and select Phone log. You can also go to Communications, click New, and select Phone log.
  2. Complete the phone log fields. You can link the phone log to a matter, a contact, or another user. Use the From and To fields to record who called whom.
  3. You can also add a time entry now or at a later time and set which users receive notifications if the phone log is updated.
    • To add time from the main Communications tab, hover over the record and click the clock icon.
  4. Click Save phone log.

 

Add time to phone logs

You can add time to a phone log when creating it or when viewing it after it has been created. To add time to an existing phone log:

  1. Go to the main Communications tab or the Communications subtab in the matter or contact.
  2. Select the Logs subtab.
  3. Find the phone log under the All or Phone quick filters.
  4. Under the Recorded time column, click Add time.
    • To add time from the main Communications tab, hover over the record and click the clock icon.
  5. Complete the time entry and click Save entry.

 

Edit phone logs

  1. Go to the main Communications tab or the Communications subtab in the matter or contact.
  2. Select the Logs subtab.
  3. Find the phone log under the All or Phone quick filters.
  4. Click Edit.
  5. Make your changes and click Save phone log.

 

Delete phone logs

Communications can only be deleted individually. Deleting in bulk is not a supported action.

Important: This is a permanent and irreversible action.

  1. Go to the main Communications tab or the Communications subtab in the matter or contact.
  2. Select the Logs subtab.
  3. Find the phone log under the All or Phone quick filters.
  4. Click the down arrow next to Edit and select Delete.
  5. When the warning prompt appears, select Delete phone log.

 

Filter phone logs

When filtering phone logs, you can filter by matter, contact, whether phone logs have time entries or not, the firm user who created the phone log, or by bill ID if the phone log is on a generated invoice.

  1. Go to the main Communications tab or the Communications subtab in the matter or contact.
  2. Click Filters.
  3. Select the appropriate parameters and click Apply filters.

 

Export phone logs

When exporting phone logs, you can choose to narrow your results by selecting specific filters (see above on filtering) and you can choose to export all columns or only those columns that are visible in the table. The exported document will be a CSV file.

  1. Go to the main Communications tab or the Communications subtab in the matter or contact.
  2. Optional: Click Filters, select the appropriate parameters, and click Apply filers.
  3. Scroll down to the bottom of the table and click Export.
  4. Select whether you want the export to show all columns or only columns you currently see.
  5. Click Export.

 

Print phone logs

If you need a physical copy of a phone log or do not need to do an export of multiple phone logs, you can print individual phone logs.

  1. Go to the main Communications tab or the Communications subtab in the matter or contact.
  2. Select the Logs subtab.
  3. Find the phone log under the All or Phone quick filters.
  4. Click the down arrow next to Edit and select Print.
